title: Rent, housing, wife's trips and his two sons
summary: Sing complains about his rent, wishes for a bigger house, mentions his wife's trips to California and his two sons.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well my rent, eat me up, $61 every month. I'm looking for the go in there one night, the roof be done fell in on me and I'm a shoe out of there, I own a house. You, you, you don't fix nothing. How many rooms you got there?
Two rooms in the kitchen. Two rooms in the kitchen?
Yeah, sixty-one rooms. I got five rooms here for seventy-five.
But I'm working. If I had five rooms in my house I'd have me a den, a bowl and everything else in there. Yeah, because you could build anything.
Yeah. Why don't you look for something better?
I'm trying to get me something to buy.
You know, between your job and what you make at Preservation Hall, you don't get to save
much money, do you? Not right now, I don't see. My money's probably going on, so my wife's been doing trips.
Oh, your wife's been making trips? Yeah. Where's she been going?

Why don't you put a piano or a trumpet in her hand and make her earn some money like Sheik does when he goes home. Yeah. How many children do you have all together? Two boys. Two boys? How old are they?
My youngest boy is thirty, my oldest boy is thirty.
